question.:question/problem:
The temperature $T(t),$ in degrees Celsius, of a compressor of a refrigerator can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{dT}{dt}=-0.09(T-20)
$$

where $t>0$ is the time, measured in minutes. If the initial temperature of the compressor is ${96}^{∘}C,$ calculate the temperature of the compressor after $12$ minutes. Round your answer to the nearest integer.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We're told that the temperature of the compressor of a refrigerator is modeled by the inhibited decay equation

$$
\frac{dT}{dt}=-0.09(T-20).
$$

First, we integrate our differential equation by separating the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dT}{T-20} & =-0.09\,dt \\ \int \frac{dT}{T-20} & =-\int 0.09\,\text{d}t \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡|T-20| & =-0.09t+C\end{aligned}
$$

Since this is the solution to an inhibited decay equation, we have $T-20>0$ for all $t>0.$
Next, we solve for $T(t),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T-20 & ={e}^{-0.09t+C} \\ T-20 & ={e}^{C}{e}^{-0.09t} \\ T-20 & =K{e}^{-0.09t} \\ T & =20+K{e}^{-0.09t}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $K={e}^{C}$ is a constant of integration. 

We're told that the initial temperature of the compressor was ${96}^{∘}C.$ So, we apply the initial condition $T(0)=96,$ and solve for $K:$

$$
\begin{aligned}96 & =20+K{e}^{0} \\ 96 & =20+K \\ K & =76\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to our initial value problem is

$$
T(t)=20+76{e}^{-0.09t}.
$$

Finally, the temperature of the compressor after $t=12$ minutes is

$$
T(12)=20+76{e}^{-0.09\cdot 12}≈{46}^{∘}\text{C},
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.
